scenes.heading: Probability review
scenes.sub: Everything you need before the rest of the chapter
scenes.say: A seventy percent chance of rain. A one in six chance of rolling a six. Probability is the maths of uncertainty, and this video pulls together the key skills you have met so far.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: The whole pizza is worth 1; your slices are a fraction of it
scenes.science: P(event) = outcomes you want ÷ all equally likely outcomes
scenes.breaks: You can see pizza slices are different sizes. Outcomes can look alike without being equally likely.
scenes.say: Think of a pizza. The whole pizza is everything that could happen, and it is worth one. The slices you want are your event. If you want three of eight equal slices, your probability is three eighths, and the rest of the pizza, five eighths, is the chance it does not happen.

scenes.heading: The two key rules
scenes.say: For equally likely outcomes, the probability of A is the number of outcomes in A divided by the total. And the chance of not A, written A dash, is one minus the probability of A.

scenes.heading: Spinners: use the angle
scenes.say: First the spinner, then its three sectors. There are three colours, but red takes up half the circle. So the chance of red is one hundred and eighty out of three hundred and sixty, which is one half, not one third. Blue is ninety out of three hundred and sixty, one quarter.
scenes.caption: There are 3 colours, but red takes up half the circle. P(red) = 180 ÷ 360 = 1/2, not 1/3. P(blue) = 90 ÷ 360 = 1/4.

scenes.heading: Two dice: 36 equally likely cells
scenes.say: For two dice, draw a six by six grid of sums. That makes thirty-six equally likely cells. Now shade the sums of nine or more: four nines, three tens, two elevens and one twelve. That is ten cells, so the probability is ten over thirty-six, which simplifies to five eighteenths.

scenes.heading: Expected number
scenes.question: The spinner is spun 200 times. How many blues do you expect? Blue came up 62 times: relative frequency?
scenes.say: Spin it two hundred times. The chance of blue is one quarter, so you expect a quarter of two hundred, which is fifty blues. Blue actually came up sixty-two times. The relative frequency is sixty-two divided by two hundred, zero point three one. That is close to zero point two five, and small differences are normal.
scenes.caption: P(blue) = 1/4, so expect 1/4 × 200 = 50 blues. Blue came up 62 times: relative frequency = 62 ÷ 200 = 0.31, close to 0.25.

points: P = outcomes wanted ÷ equally likely total
scenes.say: Quick recap. Probability is the outcomes you want over all the equally likely outcomes. Not A is one minus A. On spinners, use the angle. For two dice, use the thirty-six cell grid. And expected number is probability times trials. Now try the practice questions!
